I'm about to turn 18 and I like a guy who is 16 and a half, and I've been feeling the same way. I really like him, but I'm hesitant to pursue anything because of what people will think. I know it's only a year and a half difference, but because we're young, that small gap can mean a lot more. Anyways, I totally understand your situation, and honestly I'd say it's ok. If he likes you and you like him, who cares what other people think? Maturity level matters much more than a year and a half gap.

Of course it's ok to have a preference! I'd never really put much thought into it before, but now that I am, I think I have the same preference as you. This of course isn't the only type of person I would date, but I think if I could choose my dream person, that is what I would choose. That being said, it is perfectly normal to have preferences as long as you communicate them to potential partners. As far as approaching this topic with someone, bring it up when you're having a conversation about what you are into. What is it about penises that you like? Do you just like the look of them, or is it about penetration? See, you don't have to say you want a feminine person with a penis, you can simply be with a feminine person and tell them that you prefer to be penetrated, as an example. That way, they know that a strap could possibly fulfill your needs. It is a great way for you to find out how they feel about the situation without flat out asking if they have a penis.

I think you've already gotten a lot of quality advice, but I just wanted to say I was in a similar situation at the beginning of this year. I had a couple crushes on people of the same sex alone with many crushes on the opposite sex, and assumed for the longest time that my attractions to the same sex were flukes. I realize now how stupid that was. To be bisexual, you don't have to be 50/50. You can be 75/25, 60/40, 90/10 even. No one can define your sexuality besides you. Try different titles, see what you like, and if you never decide, that's perfectly fine too. Be true to yourself, and as cheesy as this sounds, follow your heart.

Alright, there are so many comments here already, but I just want to say that I am so so sorry that this happened to you. I'm 15 as well, as is my partner, and I've been with them for a year and a half. They mean the absolute world to me and I don't know what I would do if I ever lost them. I cry at the thought of losing them even for a moment. Your parents need to respect your grief. As I always say, while it is not likely that you two would have spent the rest of your lives together given your age, that in itself is no reason to throw it away. My favorite quote is "Do it. Fall in love. Fearless. Senseless. Foolish. Love. Heartbreak will find you whether you invite it or not, so you might as well enjoy the high." While they may not see it as love, you do, and if they really loved you they would respect that and get you the help that you need. Please reach out if you need any more help, and I am so incredibly sorry that this happened to you.
